title: 28yo M High-Voltage Electrical Injury
chiefComplaint: Electrocuted while working on a rooftop, thrown clear
background: Air conditioning installer. His aluminium ladder contacted an 11 kV overhead distribution line. Witnesses report he was rigid for several seconds, then thrown about two metres onto a concrete roof and fell a further 3 metres. Brief loss of consciousness. Colleagues began compressions before realising he had a pulse. He is 76 kg. In high-voltage injury the visible skin wounds represent a small fraction of the damage, since current follows the path of least resistance through nerve, blood vessel and muscle deep to the skin.

exam.finding: Alert but agitated and confused, in severe pain in the right arm, smell of burnt tissue, clothing charred at the right hand and left foot
Occipital scalp haematoma from the fall, no facial burns, no singed nasal hairs and no soot in the oropharynx so no inhalational injury, cervical collar in place, tympanic membranes intact
Sinus tachycardia at 124/min with occasional ventricular ectopics, blood pressure maintained, radial pulse present on the left but not palpable on the right, capillary refill 2 seconds centrally
Equal air entry, tender right ribs 6 to 8 from the fall, no surgical emphysema, no flail segment, tachypnoeic from pain and acidosis
Soft, mildly tender in the right upper quadrant, no rebound, no seatbelt sign, pelvis stable. Blunt abdominal injury from the fall must be excluded separately from the electrical injury

Deep charred contact wound over the right palm (entry) measuring 4 cm, and a similar exit wound over the left heel. Total burn surface area under 3%, which is deceptive. Right forearm is tense, swollen and hard with pain on passive finger extension

GCS 14 (E4V4M6), confused, no focal deficit centrally. Right hand is insensate over the median distribution with weak finger flexion. Peripheral nerve injury is common and may be immediate or delayed by days to weeks

investigations.name: Creatine kinase
investigations.report: Massive rhabdomyolysis. Values in high-voltage injury are frequently far higher than the visible wounds suggest, because the muscle damage is deep and extensive.

investigations.name: Urinalysis
investigations.value: Dark tea-coloured urine, dipstick blood 4+, no red cells on microscopy
investigations.report: Myoglobinuria. Dipstick positive for blood with no red cells on microscopy is the classic finding and confirms pigment nephropathy risk.

investigations.name: Potassium and creatinine
investigations.report: Hyperkalaemia from muscle breakdown with acute kidney injury. Potassium will rise further after fasciotomy releases the damaged compartment.

investigations.name: 12-Lead ECG
investigations.report: Sinus tachycardia with frequent ventricular ectopics and peaked T waves consistent with hyperkalaemia. No ST elevation. Arrhythmia is the immediate cause of death in electrical injury and 24 hours of monitoring is indicated after high-voltage exposure or loss of consciousness.

investigations.name: Blood gas and lactate
investigations.report: Metabolic acidosis from muscle necrosis and hypoperfusion.

investigations.name: CT head, cervical spine and torso
investigations.report: Small right frontal contusion without mass effect. No cervical spine injury. Right ribs 6 to 8 fractures with a small pulmonary contusion. No intra-abdominal injury. The fall must be worked up as blunt trauma in its own right.

data.label: Treat as blunt trauma as well as electrical injury
actions: Primary survey with cervical spine precautions

doseMap.Treat as blunt trauma as well as electri: The fall and the tetanic muscle contraction cause fractures and internal injury independent of the current. Focusing only on the burns misses the spine and the head

data.label: Aggressive fluid resuscitation, far beyond burn surface area formulas
actions: Do not use the Parkland formula here

doseMap.Large volume crystalloid: Target urine output 1.5-2 mL/kg/h (about 115-150 mL/h), which is roughly double the target for a thermal burn
doseMap.Do not use the Parkland formula here: Surface area based formulas grossly underestimate requirements in high-voltage injury, because the muscle damage is invisible. Titrate to urine output, not to a calculation

data.label: Treat hyperkalaemia and monitor for arrhythmia
actions: Continuous cardiac monitoring for at least 24 hours

doseMap.Calcium gluconate for ECG changes: 10 mL of 10% IV over 3 min, repeat as needed
doseMap.Continuous cardiac monitoring for at lea: Indicated after high-voltage exposure, loss of consciousness or an abnormal initial ECG. He has all three

data.label: Compartment syndrome of the right forearm
data.narrative: The forearm is tense and woody with progressive sensory loss and pain on passive stretch. The radial pulse is absent, which is a late sign. Deep muscle necrosis under intact skin is characteristic and there is no way to assess it without opening the compartment.

data.label: Urgent fasciotomy, with anticipation of a potassium surge
actions: Emergency forearm fasciotomy and carpal tunnel release

doseMap.Prepare for reperfusion hyperkalaemia: Releasing a necrotic compartment washes potassium and myoglobin into the circulation. Have calcium, insulin, dextrose and a defibrillator ready before the incision

data.label: Report the unsafe worksite and tell him he can be treated regardless of documentation status (Empathy)
data.narrative: He is 28, he is not on any formal employment contract, and his first coherent question is whether he will have to pay and whether his employer will find out. You tell him the emergency treatment is covered, that reporting the incident does not jeopardise his care, and that an aluminium ladder within reach of an 11 kV line is a fatal setup that will kill the next installer if nobody records it. You file the occupational injury report yourself. Three of his colleagues are working on the same building tomorrow.

data.label: Burns centre transfer and ongoing monitoring

doseMap.Ophthalmology review for delayed catarac: Cataract develops in a proportion of high-voltage survivors, sometimes months later, and needs baseline documentation now

data.label: Course
data.narrative: Fasciotomy releases extensive necrotic flexor muscle requiring debridement on days 2 and 4. Creatine kinase peaks at 68000 on day 2. Creatinine peaks at 3.8 mg/dL and he requires two sessions of dialysis, then recovers. The hand is salvaged but the median nerve deficit persists.

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: Discharged to rehabilitation at week 5 with skin grafting to the forearm and a persistent median nerve deficit needing tendon transfer at six months. Renal function normalises. The occupational report leads to an inspection and the removal of two more ladders from the same contractor's sites.
